answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring inbound collateral channels before an identity carries weight. Cheap keypairs can fill a meadow, yet stay mute until independent peers lock slashable funds into channels aimed at that identity, forming a public trellis of capacity peers can audit. New channels open only through a rate-limited jetty, so fresh keys cannot instantly draw liquidity. Majority weight forces the attacker to make many unaffiliated counterparties lock real capital on every fake persona; they lose that stake if it later colludes. Minting keys is cheap; inbound capital is not.
